symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit.
Leaves curl, yellow and drop early.
Cracked, corky scabs on fruit.
causes: Cool, wet spring weather; spores overwinter in fallen leaves.
organicTreatment: Spray sulfur or lime-sulfur from bud break through petal fall.
chemicalTreatment: Myclobutanil or difenoconazole during wet periods.
prevention: Prune for good airflow and sunlight.

symptoms: Purple-edged 'frog-eye' leaf spots with tan centres.
Sunken cankers on branches.
Fruit rot that turns black and mummifies.
causes: Spreads from dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit in warm, wet weather.
organicTreatment: Prune out cankers and dead wood; remove mummified fruit.
Apply copper or sulfur sprays during the growing season.
chemicalTreatment: Captan or thiophanate-methyl sprays from bloom onward.
prevention: Keep orchard free of prunings and fallen fruit.
Avoid tree stress and bark wounds.

symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface.
Small tube-like structures under the spots.
Early leaf drop and spotted fruit.
causes: Needs nearby juniper/cedar trees to complete its life cycle.
organicTreatment: Spray sulfur from pink bud stage through early summer.
chemicalTreatment: Myclobutanil or mancozeb sprays in spring.
prevention: Avoid planting junipers near apple trees.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or curling.
prevention: Keep up regular pruning, watering and orchard hygiene.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or curling.
White powdery patches on young leaves.
Leaves curl upward and become distorted.
causes: Warm days, cool nights and high humidity.
organicTreatment: Spray sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or neem oil.
chemicalTreatment: Myclobutanil, trifloxystrobin or other labelled mildew fungicides.
prevention: Remove water sprouts and keep good airflow.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or curling.
prevention: Keep up regular pruning and watering.

symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-tan lesions between leaf veins.
Lesions merge and kill large leaf areas.
causes: Warm, humid weather and corn residue left on the field.
organicTreatment: Remove or plough under infected residue.
Rotate with non-host crops for at least one season.
chemicalTreatment: Azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin or propiconazole at first lesions on upper leaves.
prevention: Rotate crops and avoid continuous corn.

symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Leaves yellow and dry with heavy infection.
causes: Cool, humid weather; spores blow in on the wind.
chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb, azoxystrobin or propiconazole when pustules appear before tasselling.
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak rust periods.

symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions (2.5-15 cm).
Lesions start on lower leaves and move up.
causes: Moderate temperatures with long periods of leaf wetness.
chemicalTreatment: Propiconazole, azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin when lesions reach the ear leaf.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no lesions or pustules.
prevention: Keep up balanced fertilizing and crop rotation.

symptoms: Round tan leaf spots with dark borders and black dots.
Berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
causes: Warm, wet weather; overwinters in mummified berries.
organicTreatment: Remove mummified berries and infected canes.
Spray copper or sulfur from early shoot growth.
chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb, captan or myclobutanil from bud break until fruit colours.

symptoms: Tiger-stripe yellow/red patches between leaf veins.
Dark spots on berries; sudden wilting of vines.
causes: Wood-rotting fungi (Phaeomoniella, Phaeoacremonium) entering through pruning wounds.
organicTreatment: Cut out and burn infected wood well below symptoms.
chemicalTreatment: No curative spray; protect pruning wounds with labelled wound-protectant fungicides.

symptoms: Irregular dark red-brown spots on leaves.
Spots merge, leaves dry and drop early.
causes: Warm, humid conditions late in the season.
chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb or carbendazim sprays at first symptoms.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or discoloration.
prevention: Keep up canopy management and vineyard hygiene.

symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellow mottling on leaves.
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green.
causes: Candidatus Liberibacter bacteria spread by the Asian citrus psyllid.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected trees to protect others.
Control psyllids with neem oil or horticultural oil.
chemicalTreatment: No cure; control psyllids with imidacloprid or other labelled insecticides.

symptoms: Small dark water-soaked leaf spots that fall out ('shot holes').
Pitted, cracked spots on fruit.
organicTreatment: Spray copper during dormancy and early season.
chemicalTreatment: Copper hydroxide or oxytetracycline sprays (where permitted).

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or holes.
prevention: Keep up regular pruning and watering.

symptoms: Small yellow-green spots that turn brown with a yellow halo.
Leaves drop early; raised scabby spots on fruit.
causes: Warm, humid weather and splashing water.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected plant parts.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering and rotate crops.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or discoloration.
prevention: Continue current watering and fertilizing practices.

symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-board look) on older leaves.
Yellowing around the spots.
causes: Warm, humid weather and stressed plants.
prevention: Keep plants well fed and watered at the base.

symptoms: Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves.
White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid weather.
Tubers rot with reddish-brown flesh.
causes: Cool, wet weather; spreads very fast.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering; hill up soil around plants.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or patches.
prevention: Continue crop rotation and good watering practice.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or discoloration.
Leaves are evenly green with no spots or discoloration.
White powdery spots on leaves and stems.
Leaves yellow, dry and die early.
causes: Warm, dry days with humid nights and crowded plants.
organicTreatment: Spray potassium bicarbonate, sulfur or neem oil.

symptoms: Many small dark purple spots on leaves.
Spots merge and leaves look scorched and dry.
causes: Warm, wet weather; spreads by water splash.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest.
prevention: Use drip irrigation and renew beds regularly.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots.
Small dark greasy spots on leaves, often with yellow halos.
Raised scabby spots on fruit.
causes: Warm, wet weather and splashing water.

symptoms: Dark spots with concentric rings on older leaves.
Yellowing leaves that drop from the bottom up.
causes: Warm, humid weather; spores live in soil and debris.
organicTreatment: Spray copper or Bacillus subtilis based fungicide.
prevention: Rotate crops and stake plants for airflow.

symptoms: Large greasy dark patches on leaves.
White mould under leaves in humid weather.
Firm brown patches on fruit.
causes: Cool, wet weather; spreads very fast.
organicTreatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
prevention: Keep leaves dry and space plants well.

symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaf surface.
Olive-green to grey velvety mould underneath.
organicTreatment: Remove infected leaves; spray copper fungicide.

symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres.
Lower leaves yellow and drop.
causes: Warm, wet weather; spreads by water splash.
prevention: Mulch and water at the base.
Rotate crops and clear plant debris.

symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckles on leaves.
Fine webbing under leaves; leaves turn bronze and dry.
organicTreatment: Spray leaves with water, neem oil or insecticidal soap.

symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and rings.
Spots on leaves, stems and fruit.
prevention: Improve airflow by pruning and staking.

symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow at the edges.
Plants are stunted with few fruits.
causes: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus spread by whiteflies.
organicTreatment: Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps and neem oil.
chemicalTreatment: No cure; control whiteflies with imidacloprid or other labelled insecticides.

symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves.
Leaves curl or look fern-like; plants are stunted.
causes: Spreads by touch, tools and infected seed.
organicTreatment: Wash hands and disinfect tools after handling plants.
chemicalTreatment: No chemical cure for the virus.
prevention: Use resistant varieties and certified seed.

symptoms: Leaves are evenly green with no spots or curling.
prevention: Continue current watering and fertilizing practices.

symptoms: Not a recognizable plant or crop leaf.
causes: Camera pointed at a non-plant object.
prevention: Ensure the crop leaf is clearly visible and well-lit.
